claim: The ge in geri cannot be built from the 下 card, which teaches only shita, and the back does not say this reading is new, so a learner reading it as shitari thinks they misremembered the kanji card.
evidence: 下痢 back: 'Says: geri'. Lesson 4 下 back: 'Says: shita'. Earlier 下 words: 地下鉄 chikatetsu, 下手 heta; none uses ge.
fix: Add ge to the 下 card's readings, or a note on 下痢 that 下 reads ge here.
verdictReason: Not a finding. 下 (chapter-5 r-a6caf2effb1c) is the WORD した 'Under', a voiced word card by reading rule 4 (the word wins over the character), so its romaji is the word's reading, not a list of the kanji's readings. A reading card has no Note field by design (docs/designs/reading-decks/04-card-rules.md, 'Never: ... the Note field'), so neither fix exists in this deck. The back 'geri' is the book's げり; a compound's reading is learned from the compound card.

evidence: 二日酔い back: 'Says: futsukayoi'. Lesson 4 二 back: 'Says: ni / futa'. 日 back: 'ni, nichi, nit-, jitsu / bi, hi, ka'. No 二日 card in the ledger.
fix: Add a note that 二日 reads futsuka (the 2nd, or two days) as a whole word.
verdictReason: Not a finding. 二 (chapter-5 r-1d5639f716b6) is a character card whose readings are the official list (ni / futa; src/reading/joyoReadings.js). ふつか is a special whole-word reading of 二日 (常用漢字表 付表), not a reading of 二, so there is nothing true to add to that card, and a reading card has no Note field by design (04-card-rules.md). The back 'futsukayoi' is the book's ふつかよい.

claim: 'Physician' reads as a plain synonym of the 医者 'Doctor' the learner already knows, and nothing says 内科 is internal medicine, while the same chapter glosses 眼科 and 歯科 as the field or clinic, so the learner cannot tell what 内 adds or why 科 is sometimes a person and sometimes a department.
evidence: 内科 back: 'Answer: Physician'. Lesson 10 医者 back: 'Answer: Doctor'. Lesson 6 科 back: 'Course; department'. This unit: 眼科 'Ophthalmology (eye clinic)', 歯科 'Dentistry (dental clinic)', 外科 'Surgeon'.
fix: Gloss it 'Internal medicine; physician' so the back names the department the kanji spell.
verdictReason: The card is faithful to the book: Useful Expressions, Doctor's office, prints '内科 physician' (beside '外科 surgeon'), and the book is respected. 'Physician' is also distinct from the chapter-11 医者 'Doctor', so rule 9 (English tells the card apart) holds. The 眼科/歯科 glosses differ in style only because the deck split 眼科（目医者）and 歯科（歯医者）into two cards each and had to keep their English apart; that is not a defect in 内科.

claim: The Useful Expressions clinic exchange teaches 保険証, 痛み止め and 食後 with translations, and none of the three has a card anywhere in the collection.
evidence: Book, Useful Expressions, At the Clinic's Reception: "保険証を見せてください。 Please show me your health insurance certificate.", "痛み止めです。 These are painkillers.", "食後に飲んでください。 Please take one after meals." candidates/coverage.json notes: "Excluded the 'At the Clinic's Reception' dialogue (sentences, not a set-expression list)". No card with target 保険証, 痛み止め or 食後 exists in any unit.
fix: Owner decides whether the clinic exchange is a set-expression list; if it is, card 保険証 "Health insurance certificate", 痛み止め "Painkiller" and 食後 "After meals" in chapter-13.
verdictReason: Verified: no card with target 保険証, 痛み止め or 食後 in any cards.json of the collection. But the three words occur only in the 'At the Clinic's Reception' dialogue (two speakers, full sentences), not in any vocabulary table or set-expression list; reading rule 1 excludes a word that only appears in a dialogue, and candidates/coverage.json records the exclusion with that reason. The exclusion is sound.

claim: The Culture Note glosses 台風 and 梅雨 as words, but the coverage pass dropped them along with the place names; 台風 is carded nowhere and 梅雨 not until chapter-22.
evidence: Book, Culture Notes (日本の気候): "the arrival of the rainy season ( 梅雨 )", "Typhoons ( 台風 ) make occasional landfalls". candidates/coverage.json: "Excluded ... culture-note prose place names/terms (梅雨, 台風, 札幌, 東京, 那覇)". Only 梅雨 card: chapter-22 r-7d72598db4ca "Rainy season (in Japan, early summer)" (Reading and Writing 9).
fix: Card 台風 "Typhoon" in chapter-13, and consider moving the 梅雨 card here, or accept culture-note glosses as out of scope.
verdictReason: Verified: 台風 has no card anywhere and 梅雨 is carded only in chapter-22. But the Culture Note is prose with a parenthetical kanji, not a vocabulary table, set-expression list or kanji table, so rule 1 does not card it; candidates/coverage.json records the exclusion. 梅雨 is carded where the book teaches it as vocabulary (chapter-22, Reading and Writing 9), which is where rule 1 puts it.

claim: The romaji '~dai' carries the book's 〜 placeholder (as an ASCII tilde) although the target 代 and the TTS text だい dropped it, and the English 'Charge; fee' gives no slot marker, so the back reads as if part of the word is missing.
evidence: cards.json r-b5a9258cf7d9: target 代, ttsText だい, pronunciation '~dai'; rendered back 'Says: ~dai'. Book vocabulary: '〜だい 〜代 charge; fee'. Comparable suffix cards in chapter-12 drop the tilde and mark the slot in the English: 点 'ten' / '. . . points', 行目 'gyōme' / 'Line number . . .'; chapter-5 時間 '~jikan' and chapter-11 方面 '〜hōmen', 番線 '〜bansen', 週間 '〜shūkan', 行き '〜iki', か月 '〜kagetsu' keep it. Preflight's romaji-style check passes the card, so this is not already reported.
fix: Change the pronunciation to 'dai'. Optionally gloss it '... charge; ... fee' so the slot is marked in the English the way chapter-12's 点 and 行目 do; whichever convention is chosen should be applied to the chapter-5 and chapter-11 tilde cards in the same sweep.
verdictReason: Checked cards.json: pronunciation is '~dai' while target is 代 and ttsText だい, and the book prints 〜代. Both roles saw the same defect; merged. The collection is inconsistent (chapter-12 drops the tilde, chapter-5 and chapter-11 keep it), and preflight does not catch it, so a fixer can act on it. Polish is the right weight: the reading is still correct.
